name: Dash & Driver Controls
description: Driver display/logger, CAN keypad or switch panel, ignition and start controls, steering-wheel buttons via quick-release connector or wireless system, shift lights, warning lamps and rotary map/traction switches. Replaces the factory IPC, BCM-driven switches and infotainment.

components.name: Dash display / display-logger
components.description: Colour TFT display showing rpm, gear, speed, lap/delta, temps/pressures and alarms; most race dashes also log (the logger heart of the data system) and drive shift lights. Receives ECU, PDM, ABS, GPS and sensor data over CAN.
components.location: In front of the driver behind the steering wheel, on a bracket from the dash bar (x≈1.15, y≈0.85, z=+0.37).

factory.name: GM instrument panel cluster (IPC) + Head-up display (ZL1)
factory.notes: Requires BCM/GMLAN; removed in a standalone build.

raceOptions.name: MoTeC C187 display logger
raceOptions.notes: 7 in colour, 4 CAN buses, 10 AV / 4 AT inputs (20/8 with I/O upgrade 29900), 250 MB logging, 79-pin Autosport connector.

raceOptions.name: MoTeC C127 display
raceOptions.notes: 7 in, 2 CAN, logging optional (120 MB). Listed obsolete by MoTeC – buy C1212/C1812 class replacement.

raceOptions.name: AiM PDM32 with 6 in or 10 in display (combined PDM/logger/dash)

hardware.item: Dash mounting screws (to bracket via isolators)
hardware.spec: M4 or M5 screws into display inserts

hardware.item: Dash bracket clamps to dash bar
hardware.spec: Tube clamps for 38–45 mm cage tube, M6

installNotes: Mount where it is visible through the wheel at full belt tension; avoid glare angle.
Configure channels, alarms and shift-light thresholds before first start.
Set logger trigger (e.g. speed > 30 km/h or rpm > 500).
inspection: Download data after every session; check alarms log.

images.title: MoTeC C187 product page – 196.2 x 122.5 x 24.9 mm, 79-pin Autosport
HP Academy: MoTeC C127 / C187 release (LED layout)

modelRef.features: Black bezel, wide 7" screen low in the face, row of 10 RGB shift LEDs above the screen, 3 alarm LEDs down each side, single 79-pin Autosport connector at the rear, 4 rear threaded mounts. Tilted back ~15° toward the driver.

components.name: CAN keypad / switch panel
components.description: Sealed CAN keypad replacing toggle switches: ignition, start, fuel pumps prime, fans override, lights, rain light, wipers, pit limiter, cool-suit, radio, dash page, alarm acknowledge. Each button LED shows PDM output state. Alternatively the Cartek PDP-16 has its own integrated button panel.
components.location: Center console/dash center, reachable with belts tight (x≈1.15, y≈0.70, z≈+0.05).

raceOptions.name: MoTeC 15 Button CAN Keypad
raceOptions.notes: IP67, 3x5 layout, 3 LEDs per button, 4-wire CAN.

raceOptions.name: Grayhill 3K 15-key CAN keypad (J1939)
raceOptions.notes: Illuminated, IP67; commonly used with PDMs supporting J1939/CANopen keypads.

installNotes: Label buttons with durable inserts; put IGN and START on the bottom row and keep a hardwired backup for IGN if rules/experience demand.

modelRef.dimensions: 129.5 x 89.5 x 15.7 mm without connector, 175 g, 5 x 3 buttons.
modelRef.features: Black rubber keys in a 5-wide x 3-high grid, each with a 3-LED bar and legend label; moulded DT04-4P connector on the back; IP67.

components.name: Ignition switch & start button (hardwired)
components.description: Guarded ignition toggle and a momentary start button, either as keypad inputs or hardwired to PDM switch inputs. A hardwired ignition input is a robust fallback if CAN is lost.

raceOptions.name: Guarded toggle + sealed momentary push button

modelRef.features: Aluminium plate with red flip-guarded ignition toggle and a momentary start button.

components.name: Steering-wheel buttons & quick-release electrical connector
components.description: Buttons on the race wheel for radio PTT, pit limiter, dash page/lap marker, flash/high beam, and ack. Signals pass through a quick-release hub with integrated multi-pin connector, or via an infrared wireless system so no wires cross the quick release.

factory.name: GM steering-wheel controls via clockspring (LIN to BCM)

raceOptions.name: Cartek Wireless Steering Wheel Control System
raceOptions.notes: 8-button IR wheel panel, receiver with 10 A relay channels (momentary/latching/flashing); 6 x 70 mm hub pattern.

hardware.notes: Wheel-to-hub bolts belong to steering system.

installNotes: Route the column-side lead with a coil cord or fixed clamp so it cannot wrap at full lock.
inspection: Connector pins clean; all buttons respond.

modelRef.dimensions: Button panel ~150 x 90 mm on the wheel face (estimated).
modelRef.features: 8 sealed push buttons (4 each side of the hub), coloured caps, IR transmitter pod behind.

components.name: Shift lights
components.description: Sequential LED shift lights (integrated in the C187/C127 top LED bar or an external CAN shift-light module) driven from rpm and gear; also used for alarm flashing and pit-limiter indication.
components.location: Top of dash display / dash bar in line of sight (x≈1.14, y≈0.93, z=+0.37).

raceOptions.name: Integrated in MoTeC C1xx (16 RGB LEDs on C127)

hardware.item: External shift-light module screws (if not integrated)

installNotes: Set gear-dependent shift points from dyno/accel data.

modelRef.dimensions: Integrated in the C127/C187 bezel: 10 LEDs across the top + 3 per side.
modelRef.features: LED row above the screen; same box as the dash display.

components.name: Hardwired warning lamps (oil pressure / master alarm)
components.description: Large, bright LED lamps for low oil pressure and master alarm, driven by a dash/PDM output – visible even if the dash page is changed. Cheap insurance for a dry-sump race engine.
components.location: Dash bar either side of display.

modelRef.dimensions: 22 mm panel-mount LED pilot lamps, bezel Ø~28 mm, ~40 mm deep.
modelRef.features: Chrome bezel, red domed lens, black threaded body with jam nut.

components.name: Rotary switches (traction control, ABS map, fuel map)
components.description: 12-position rotary switches read by the ECU (analogue input) or by the ABS (Bosch ABS M5 uses a 12-position switch or CAN for map selection).

factory.name: GM Performance Traction Management / drive-mode selector (BCM)

inspection: Each position reads correctly in data.

modelRef.dimensions: 12-position rotary switch, knob Ø~30 mm, ~50 mm overall depth (estimated).
modelRef.features: Black knob with white pointer, chrome jam nut, black body with solder pins.

components.name: Factory body electronics (BCM, IPC, radio, airbag) – removal/retention
components.description: Gen 6 body control module (BCM), instrument cluster, infotainment, airbag SDM, keyless entry, column modules. With a Chevrolet Performance controller kit or race standalone ECU the engine runs without them; removing them saves weight and failure points. Retaining OE ABS/stability and electric power steering requires those modules (and their CAN messages) to be satisfied – a key decision tied to the steering and brakes systems.
components.location: Throughout the factory dash/body (removed in phase 1 strip).

factory.name: GM BCM / IPC / SDM / radio
factory.notes: Global A modules are VIN-matched; they cannot simply be swapped between vehicles.

installNotes: Decide early: OE EPS + ABS retained (needs GMLAN data such as vehicle speed/engine-run) vs. race ABS (Bosch M5) and hydraulic/ standalone-EPS steering.
